title: Relief Against a Granite Ridge Restoration Charge for How the Pass Record Was Opened
content:
How a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass record was opened, together with how long the application has stood, relieves part of the charge for restoring scanning privileges.

Where the pass record was opened as a carry-over from the preceding season and the application was recorded at least 60 days before the handling date, three twentieths of the charge is relieved, which is a rate of 15 per cent. Where the pass record was opened as a renewal of a pass held in the preceding season and the application was recorded at least 60 days before the handling date, a tenth of the charge is relieved, which is a rate of 10 per cent. In any other case no relief is given on this head, and that is so both where the record was opened on neither footing and where it was opened on one of them but the application has stood for fewer than 60 days.

The count of 60 days runs from the day the application was recorded on the pass record, not from the day the pass became scannable. The two ways a record may have been opened are alternatives: a record is opened as a carry-over or as a renewal, and never on both footings at once, so the two rates never fall to be added together.

Taken at the threshold, a record opened as a carry-over whose application was recorded 59 days before the handling date attracts no relief on this head, while the same record at 60 days attracts three twentieths of the charge. A record opened as a renewal at 60 days attracts a tenth of the charge instead, and at 59 days none.

Worked on a hypothetical record: a Granite Ridge Collective Unlimited Pass opened as a renewal with the application recorded on 1 October. On a handling date of 15 December the application has stood 75 days, so a tenth of the charge is relieved. Had the record been opened as a carry-over from the preceding season with the same dates, three twentieths of the charge would be relieved instead.
